The film exposes properly on the shot
Penetrant can enter, and false marks are avoided
distractors: Cleaning is not magnetizing.
Couplant is for UT.
No film is involved.
content.explanation: Pre-cleaning removes coatings and contaminants that would block penetrant or cause false indications.

content.stem: Dwell time lets the penetrant:
options: Evaporate completely from the surface as a rule
Bond the coating onto the weld metal
Cool the weld down after the pass
Seep into the surface-breaking discontinuities
distractors: Full evaporation defeats the test.
It does not bond coatings.
It does not cool the weld.
content.explanation: Dwell allows penetrant to enter open discontinuities before excess removal.

content.stem: Developer is applied to:
options: Add more penetrant onto the surface as a rule
Magnetize the part before the test
Couple sound into the weld metal
Draw penetrant out into a visible indication
distractors: It does not add penetrant.
It is not magnetizing.
It is not couplant.
content.explanation: Developer blots trapped penetrant to the surface to form a visible indication.

content.stem: A relevant PT indication comes from:
options: A scratch dragged across the developer itself
Penetrant bleeding from a real discontinuity
A piece of lint resting on the surface
A water spot left during the cleaning
distractors: Developer scratches are non-relevant.
Lint is non-relevant.
Water spots are non-relevant.
content.explanation: Relevant indications come from penetrant trapped in actual discontinuities.

content.stem: A crack revealed by PT is:
options: Acceptable on the part whenever it is faint
Rejectable wherever it appears on the weld
Acceptable as long as it sits off the cap
Classed as a non-relevant indication
distractors: Faintness does not exempt it.
Location does not exempt it.
A crack is relevant.
content.explanation: Cracks are rejectable under API 1104; the only allowance is a crater or star crack up to 5/32 in. (4 mm) (9.5).

content.stem: Visible dye penetrant indications are read under:
options: Total darkness across the work area
Adequate white light on the surface
Ultraviolet light only on the part
Any ambient light level at all
distractors: Visible dye needs white light.
UV is for fluorescent penetrant.
Light level matters.
content.explanation: Visible dye is evaluated under adequate white light.

content.stem: Relevant indications found at Level I are:
options: Recorded for the later evaluation step
Wiped away from the part surface
Reported only verbally to the next hand
Left for the next crew to handle
distractors: Indications are documented first.
Records are written.
Recording is not deferred.
content.explanation: Relevant indications are recorded for Level II/company evaluation.

content.stem: Acceptance criteria are applied by the:
options: The Level I operator running the test
The penetrant supplier providing the kit
The Level II evaluator or the company
The pipe mill that supplied the joint
distractors: Level I records, not dispositions.
Suppliers do not interpret.
The mill supplies pipe.
content.explanation: Evaluation against the criteria is a Level II/company function.

content.stem: A PT indication exceeding the criteria is a:
options: Non-relevant indication on the part
Discontinuity found along the weld
Defect
Developer mark left on the surface
distractors: A non-relevant indication is screened out.
A discontinuity may be acceptable.
A developer mark is non-relevant.
content.explanation: A discontinuity is a defect only when it exceeds the criteria.

content.stem: A PT-rejected area after repair is:
options: Re-examined to the same method and criteria
Accepted on the strength of the repair note
Judged the second time by relaxed limits
Exempt from re-test once it is repaired
distractors: A note is not re-inspection.
Limits do not relax.
Re-examination is required.
content.explanation: The repair is re-inspected to the same basis.

content.stem: PT rather than MT is chosen when the part is:
options: Non-ferromagnetic, such as aluminum alloys
Ferromagnetic and able to hold a field itself
Always coated before the test begins
Always of a thick wall section
distractors: Ferromagnetic parts can use MT.
Coating blocks PT too.
Thickness is not the selector.
content.explanation: PT covers materials that cannot be magnetized.

content.stem: PT for API 1104 compliance is performed by personnel who are:
options: Qualified and certified for the PT method
Members of the welding crew on the spread
Chosen by lottery among the available hands
Approved by the coating crew on the line
distractors: Welders are not the NDT authority.
Qualification is not by chance.
Coaters do not certify PT.
content.explanation: Examinations are performed by qualified, certified PT personnel.
